answer: In a bonded PoA system, each identity escrows collateral, and correlated equivocation by k coordinated identities triggers penalties proportional to k², reflecting the pairwise links exposed among them. Detection also applies a compounding capital-loss multiplier, so operating a sybil swarm risks exponentially greater loss as penalties and asymmetric depreciation accumulate. A relic key, willow-like split in identity, or pulse of activity cannot hide shared control.
